item.description: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) remains a major threat to poultry production worldwide, with the GI-23 lineage emerging as one of the most epidemiologically relevant variants in recent years. item.title: Temperature-dependent effects of post-exercise cold-water immersion on recovery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: On average, CWI was associated with reductions in DOMS, CK, and Mb, although substantial heterogeneity and wide prediction intervals indicate that these effects may not be consistently reproduced across settings. Numerically larger reductions in DOMS were observed at approximately 10-15 °C than at ≈5 °C, but neither subgroup analysis nor meta-regression confirmed a temperature-dependent effect. No water-temperature range can currently be considered superior.

item.description: Solid electrolytes (SEs) are central to next-generation metal batteries, yet their discovery remains constrained by fragmented data, limited transferability of simulations, and slow experimental iteration. Unlike catalysis, where surface reactivity dominates, SEs require simultaneous optimization of bulk ion transport, defect chemistry, mechanical integrity, and interfacial stability. item.title: Incidence and Characteristics of Adverse Events: The 2024 Patient Safety Incidents Inquiry in Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: Using a standardized three-stage medical record review, the 2024 Patient Safety Incident Inquiry provides updated descriptive baseline data on confirmed adverse events across tertiary and general hospitals in Korea. These findings may support institutional patient safety improvement efforts and inform national patient safety planning.

item.title: Screening for Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Sepsis Using a Smartphone ECG Analysis Application: A Multicenter Validation Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: AI-driven ECG analysis via a smartphone app provided a rapid, accessible, and accurate screening tool for LV dysfunction in sepsis and outperformed NT-proBNP. Its high NPV suggests potential utility for early risk stratification and for informing cautious hemodynamic management, although prospective studies are needed to define its role in sepsis treatment protocols.

item.title: Experience-based recommendations for the diagnosis and management of early-stage nail unit melanoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Early diagnosis and treatment of nail unit melanoma at the in situ or minimally invasive stage (IA/IB) are associated with high cure rates. In contrast, advanced disease with deep invasion or metastasis carries a poor prognosis-therefore, timely recognition and intervention are essential to optimize outcomes.
